root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence does not establish an independent root-level semantic principle beyond the lexical field of the frog and its related derived usages.
root_idea.development: The packet documents a concrete animal noun together with derived descriptions, bodily usages, figurative idiom, astronomical names, and an equine anatomical term, but supplies no Maqāyīs or Quran-focused root-development discussion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular Classical Arabic citation form; the Quranic occurrence itself is the plural ضَفَادِع.

senses.definition: Frog; in the Quranic occurrence, the plural frogs.
senses.usage_conditions: The attested Quranic form is the plural ضَفَادِع, referring to frogs as the reptile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Classical zoological descriptions distinguish a river or water-toad and a land-toad, the latter associated with caverns and caves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive specialization of the frog/toad noun; the medicinal and magical properties reported for these species are traditional lore rather than additional lexical meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to contain or abound in frogs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Predicated of water or a body of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man, to shrink or become contracted.
Of a man, to void excrement, especially thin excrement.
Of a man, to emit wind audibly from the anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily-use verb describing audible anal flatulence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An idiom meaning that he was or became hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative expression literally describing the croaking of the frogs of one's belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Names of two stars: the bright star at the mouth of Piscis Austrinus and a star on the southern fork of Cetus's tail.
The frog: a bone or horny substance inside a horse's hoof, in its sole.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive plural form applied to waters containing many frogs.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Three bodily verb usages are represented separately.
Core frog noun and its Classical zoological species specialization.
Descriptive form for waters containing frogs.

cautions: The public headword is normalized to the singular ضِفْدِع; Classical sources also record the vocalic variants ضَفْدَع and ضُفْدَع.
The Quranic occurrence is a plural noun, while the Classical evidence includes zoological specializations and several derived or figurative usages.
